territorial_scope.description: Federal civil tort applying to any person whose conduct is in or affects interstate or foreign commerce.

evidence.quote: in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Proposed federal private tort: any person who uses or otherwise exploits an individual's covered data without express, prior consent is liable to that individual, including via generative AI training. Provides a consent defense and makes predispute arbitration agreements unenforceable for such claims. No effective date stated.
summary.long: The bill, the AI Accountability and Personal Data Protection Act, would create a federal civil tort. Under Section 3, any person who, in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce, appropriates, uses, collects, processes, sells or otherwise exploits an individual's covered data without express, prior consent is liable to that individual in civil action; aiders and abettors are also liable. Covered data includes personally identifiable information, identifiers, geolocation, biometric, behavioral and inferred data; exploitation includes training a generative AI system used by its provider and generating covered data about an individual. Remedies include the greater of actual damages, treble profits or $1,000, punitive damages, injunctive relief and attorney's fees. Consent is an affirmative defense but is invalid if obtained through coercion, deception, or as a condition of a product or service beyond what is reasonably necessary; third-party consent requires separate, specific and affirmatively presented disclosure. Predispute arbitration agreements and joint-action waivers are unenforceable for such claims, and courts decide applicability; Section 4 preserves state laws and sets a minimum standard. The text states no effective date and no public enforcement authority.

relations.note: Sec. 3(c)(1) applies notwithstanding the Federal Arbitration Act: predispute arbitration agreements and predispute joint-action waivers are not valid or enforceable for claims under this Act.

evidence.quote: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, including chapter 1 of title 9, United States Code (commonly known as the “Federal Arbitration Act”)

thresholds.variable_text: statutory minimum compensatory damages (floor in greater-of formula)
thresholds.consequence: An individual prevailing in a civil action may recover compensatory damages equal to the greater of actual damages, treble profits, or $1,000.
thresholds.conditions: Individual prevailing in a civil action under Sec. 3(b)(1); compensatory damages are the greatest of the three listed measures.
